claim: UHRF1 is a histone- and DNA-binding RING E3 ubiquitin ligase that recruits DNMT1 to sites of newly replicated DNA through ubiquitylation of histone H3.
source: The epigenetic inheritance of DNA methylation requires UHRF1, a histone- and DNA-binding RING E3 ubiquitin ligase that recruits DNMT1 to sites of newly replicated DNA through ubiquitylation of histone H3.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work establishing UHRF1's role in DNA methylation inheritance.

claim: UHRF1 binds DNA with selectivity towards hemi-methylated CpGs (HeDNA).
source: UHRF1 binds DNA with selectivity towards hemi-methylated CpGs (HeDNA)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and citations to prior structural studies.

claim: The interaction of UHRF1 with HeDNA is required for DNA methylation.
source: the interaction of UHRF1 with HeDNA is required for DNA methylation
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic complementation experiments shown in Figure 1C demonstrating that HeDNAmut cannot rescue DNA methylation loss.

claim: HeDNA recognition is dispensable for UHRF1 chromatin interaction.
source: the interaction of UHRF1 with HeDNA is required for DNA methylation but is dispensable for chromatin interaction
evidence: This claim is supported by chromatin association assays in Figure 1D showing that HeDNAmut retains chromatin binding.

claim: Chromatin interaction of UHRF1 is governed by reciprocal positive cooperativity between the UHRF1 histone- and DNA-binding domains.
source: chromatin interaction, which is governed by reciprocal positive cooperativity between the UHRF1 histone- and DNA-binding domains
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding assays shown in Figure 2 demonstrating enhanced binding when both ligands are present.

claim: HeDNA recognition activates UHRF1 ubiquitylation towards multiple lysines on the H3 tail adjacent to the UHRF1 histone-binding site.
source: HeDNA recognition activates UHRF1 ubiquitylation towards multiple lysines on the H3 tail adjacent to the UHRF1 histone-binding site.
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assays in Figure 4 and mass spectrometry data in Figure 6 identifying multiple ubiquitylation sites on H3.

claim: UHRF1 plays a central role in DNMT1-directed DNA methylation maintenance during DNA replication.
source: The E3 ubiquitin ligase UHRF1 (ubiquitin-like, containing PHD and RING finger domains 1) is one such multi-domain epigenetic regulator (Figure 1A) that plays a central role in DNMT1-directed DNA methylation maintenance during DNA replication (Bostick et al., 2007; Sharif et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies establishing UHRF1's role in DNA methylation maintenance.

claim: UHRF1 TTD-PHD has reader activity towards the N-terminus of histone H3 when it is di- and tri-methylated at lysine 9 (H3K9me2/me3).
source: It does so in part through the reader activity of its linked TTD-PHD (tandem Tudor and plant homeodomain) towards the N-terminus of histone H3 when it is di- and tri-methylated at lysine 9 (H3K9me2/me3) (Arita et al., 2012; Rothbart et al., 2013, 2012)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior structural and biochemical studies.

claim: UHRF1 RING domain mediates catalysis of H3K18 and H3K23 ubiquitylation that promotes DNMT1 association with H3.
source: through RING (really interesting new gene) domain-mediated catalysis of H3K18 and H3K23 ubiquitylation that promotes DNMT1 association with H3 (Nishiyama et al., 2013; Qin et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies demonstrating UHRF1's ubiquitin ligase activity and its role in DNMT1 recruitment.

claim: Full-length UHRF1 displayed a 10- to 20-fold preference for HeDNA over UnDNA.
source: UHRF1 displayed a 10- to 20-fold preference for HeDNA over UnDNA
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Full-length UHRF1 displayed a 5- to 10-fold preference for HeDNA over SyDNA.
source: a 5- to 10-fold preference for HeDNA over SyDNA (Figure 1B; left panel)
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The G448D mutation (DNAmut) disrupts all DNA-binding by UHRF1.
source: G448D (DNAmut) disrupts all DNA-binding (Figure 1B; middle panel) by installing a negatively charged residue at a position that contacts the DNA backbone (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 1B and structural information in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The N489A mutation (HeDNAmut) disrupts only HeDNA-sensing by UHRF1.
source: N489A (HeDNAmut), harbored within the NKR finger that contacts the unmethylated cytosine opposite the methylated base (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), disrupts only HeDNA-sensing (Figure 1B; right panel)
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 1B showing selective loss of HeDNA binding while retaining UnDNA binding.

claim: The DNA binding affinity of UHRF1 is exquisitely sensitive to small perturbations in salt concentration, with a nearly 500-fold affinity difference for HeDNA between 50 mM and 150 mM NaCl.
source: We also observed that the DNA binding affinity of UHRF1 was exquisitely sensitive to small perturbations in salt concentration; we measured a nearly 500-fold affinity difference for HeDNA between 50 mM and 150 mM NaCl (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Global DNA methylation levels were significantly reduced following stable knockdown of endogenous UHRF1 by shRNA.
source: Consistent with our previous observations (Rothbart et al., 2013, 2012), global DNA methylation levels were significantly reduced following stable knockdown of endogenous UHRF1 by shRNA (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1C and citations to prior studies.

claim: DNA methylation was restored by reintroduction of a wild-type UHRF1 transgene.
source: DNA methylation was restored by reintroduction of a wild-type UHRF1 transgene
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1C showing rescue of 5mC levels.

claim: HeDNAmut UHRF1 could not rescue DNA methylation loss in cells despite retaining its ability to bind DNA.
source: HeDNAmut could not rescue DNA methylation loss in cells despite retaining its ability to bind DNA (Figure 1B–C)
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization data in Figure 1B showing DNA binding and immunofluorescence data in Figure 1C showing failure to rescue 5mC levels.

claim: Mutations that disrupt histone interaction through the PHD finger (H3mut), E3 ubiquitin ligase activity (RINGmut), and DNA binding (DNAmut) cannot rescue DNA methylation loss.
source: but like mutations that disrupt histone interaction through the PHD finger (H3mut; Figure 1—figure supplement 1), E3 ubiquitin ligase activity (RINGmut) and DNA binding (DNAmut), HeDNAmut could not rescue DNA methylation loss in cells
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1C showing failure of these mutants to rescue 5mC levels.

claim: Hemi-methylated DNA sensing is critical for DNA methylation maintenance.
source: These results demonstrate that in addition to the well-appreciated roles of histone-binding and ubiquitin ligase activity to the DNA methylation regulatory function of UHRF1 (Nishiyama et al., 2013; Rothbart et al., 2013, 2012), hemi-methylated DNA sensing is critical for DNA methylation maintenance.
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic complementation data in Figure 1C and citations to prior studies.

claim: Wild-type and HeDNAmut UHRF1 bound to bulk chromatin biochemically fractionated from HeLa cells.
source: Notably, unlike H3mut and DNAmut, wild-type and HeDNAmut bound to bulk chromatin biochemically fractionated from HeLa cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by chromatin association assay data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The histone- and DNA-binding domains of UHRF1 perform complementary functions to target UHRF1 to chromatin.
source: Collectively, these findings suggest that the histone- and DNA-binding domains of UHRF1 are performing complementary functions to target UHRF1 to chromatin
evidence: This claim is inferred from the differential chromatin binding behavior of various UHRF1 mutants shown in Figure 1D.

claim: HeDNA recognition provides an additional regulatory layer in the DNA methylation program beyond chromatin targeting.
source: that HeDNA recognition provides an additional regulatory layer in the DNA methylation program
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that HeDNAmut binds chromatin but cannot rescue DNA methylation.

claim: Full-length UHRF1 displayed a preference for H3K9me3 peptides over unmodified H3 peptides (H3K9un).
source: In agreement with previous analyses of the isolated TTD-PHD (Rothbart et al., 2013, 2012), full-length UHRF1 displayed a preference for H3K9me3 peptides over unmodified H3 peptides (H3K9un) (Figure 2A; top panel, see also Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2A and citations to prior studies.

claim: No binding was observed for H3mut UHRF1 to H3 peptides.
source: No binding was observed for H3mut (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: No binding was observed for wild-type UHRF1 to peptides containing an N-terminal 5-carboxyfluorecin (FAM) probe to block PHD engagement.
source: or for wild-type protein binding to peptides containing an N-terminal 5-carboxyfluorecin (FAM) probe to block PHD engagement (Figure 2A; bottom panel)
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2A showing that N-terminal FAM blocks binding.

claim: HeDNA, SyDNA, and UnDNA enhanced the interaction of UHRF1 with C-terminal FAM-labeled H3K9me3 and H3K9un peptides.
source: Histone binding measurements in the presence of 10 μM unlabeled HeDNA, SyDNA, or UnDNA enhanced the interaction with C-terminal FAM-labeled H3K9me3 and H3K9un peptides (Figure 2A; top panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2A showing enhanced histone binding in the presence of DNA.

claim: HeDNA did not enhance UHRF1 binding to N-terminal FAM-labeled peptides.
source: HeDNA did not enhance binding to N-terminal FAM-labeled peptides, indicating that the multivalent interaction of the TTD-PHD with a single H3 peptide (Rothbart et al., 2013, 2012) remained intact.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2A and citations to prior studies on multivalent binding.

claim: H3K9me3 peptide enhanced UHRF1 DNA binding affinity 5–10 fold irrespective of the methylation status on DNA.
source: Reciprocally, DNA-binding measurements in the presence of 10 μM unlabeled H3K9me3 peptide enhanced DNA binding affinity 5–10 fold irrespective of the methylation status on DNA (Figure 2B–C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-C,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2B-C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The histone- and DNA-binding modules of UHRF1 are regulated by reciprocal positive allostery.
source: Collectively, these experiments demonstrate that the histone- and DNA-binding modules of UHRF1 are regulated by reciprocal positive allostery.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2 showing mutual enhancement of binding.

claim: The extent to which H3 peptides augmented the interaction of UHRF1 with DNA was dependent on the epigenetic signature on H3.
source: In agreement with the multivalent histone engagement model of the UHRF1 TTD-PHD, the extent to which H3 peptides augmented the interaction of UHRF1 with DNA was dependent on the epigenetic signature on H3.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2B showing differential enhancement by different H3 modifications.

claim: H3K9me3 peptide showed a three-fold enhancement of UHRF1 DNA binding over H3K9un.
source: H3K9me3 peptide showed a three-fold enhancement of DNA binding over H3K9un
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2B.

claim: Asymmetric di-methylation of arginine 2 (H3R2me2a) did not enhance UHRF1 DNA binding.
source: asymmetric di-methylation of arginine 2 (H3R2me2a), which blocks the UHRF1 PHD interaction with H3 (Rajakumara et al., 2011), did not enhance DNA binding (Figure 2B)
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2B and citation to prior structural study.

claim: H3mut completely perturbed the ability of an H3K9me3 peptide to positively regulate UHRF1 DNA binding.
source: Consistently, H3mut completely perturbed the ability of an H3K9me3 peptide to positively regulate DNA binding
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2C.

claim: Linkermut exhibited a weaker enhancement of UHRF1 DNA binding in the presence of peptide than wild-type.
source: a previously characterized double mutation to the linker connecting the TTD-PHD that uncouples multivalent engagement to H3 (Linkermut) (Arita et al., 2012; Rothbart et al., 2013) exhibited a weaker enhancement of DNA binding in the presence of peptide than wild-type
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2C and citations to prior studies.

claim: DNAmut remained unable to bind DNA in the presence of H3K9me3.
source: DNAmut remained unable to bind DNA in the presence of H3K9me3 (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–E)
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2C.

claim: The DNA binding affinity of HeDNAmut was enhanced by H3K9me3, although HeDNAmut could not discriminate between UnDNA and HeDNA.
source: Conversely, the DNA binding affinity of HeDNAmut was still enhanced by H3K9me3, although HeDNAmut could not discriminate between UnDNA and HeDNA (Figure 2C)
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2C.

claim: The positive allostery between DNA- and histone-binding provides a biochemical basis for HeDNAmut retention on chromatin.
source: providing a biochemical basis for HeDNAmut retention on chromatin (Figure 1D)
evidence: This claim is inferred from the binding data in Figure 2C and chromatin association data in Figure 1D.

claim: The UHRF1 TTD-PHD associated with the SRA and SRA-RING in pull-down experiments.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, the UHRF1 TTD-PHD associated with the SRA and SRA-RING in pull-down experiments (Figure 3A)
evidence: This claim is supported by pull-down assay data in Figure 3A.

claim: The association between UHRF1 TTD-PHD and SRA-RING was perturbed in the presence of DNA, irrespective of methylation status.
source: this association was perturbed in the presence of DNA, irrespective of methylation status (Figure 3B, left)
evidence: This claim is supported by pull-down assay data in Figure 3B showing loss of interaction with DNA.

claim: SRA-RING DNAmut maintained interaction with the TTD-PHD in the presence of DNA.
source: SRA-RING DNAmut maintained interaction with the TTD-PHD in the presence of DNA (Figure 3B, right)
evidence: This claim is supported by pull-down assay data in Figure 3B showing retained interaction for DNAmut.

claim: An H3K9me2 peptide did not inhibit the interaction between the SRA and the TTD-PHD.
source: However, an H3K9me2 peptide did not inhibit the interaction between the SRA and the TTD-PHD (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by pull-down assay data in Figure 3C.

claim: The DNA-binding surface of the SRA contributes to an intramolecular interaction in a manner non-competitive with histone binding.
source: These results suggest that the DNA-binding surface of the SRA contributes to an intramolecular interaction in a manner non-competitive with histone binding.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the pull-down data in Figure 3B-C showing DNA disrupts the interaction but peptide does not.

claim: UHRF1 remained monomeric in the presence and absence of ligands as measured by analytical size exclusion chromatography, dynamic light scattering, and atomic force microscopy.
source: Indeed, UHRF1 remained monomeric and in good agreement with the expected molecular weight as measured by analytical size exclusion chromatography, dynamic light scattering, and atomic force microscopy (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by biophysical data in Figure 3D-F showing monomeric UHRF1.

claim: The histone- and DNA-binding domains of UHRF1 interact and general DNA binding releases this physical association.
source: Collectively, these results show that the histone- and DNA-binding domains of UHRF1 interact and that general DNA binding releases this physical association.
evidence: This claim is supported by pull-down data in Figure 3A-B showing interaction and its disruption by DNA.

claim: Ligand-induced intramolecular rearrangement of UHRF1 domain connectivity results in high-affinity retention of UHRF1 on chromatin through positive regulation of histone- and DNA-binding activities.
source: The data further suggest that ligand-induced intramolecular rearrangement of UHRF1 domain connectivity results in high-affinity retention of UHRF1 on chromatin through positive regulation of histone- and DNA-binding activities.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined binding and pull-down data showing conformational changes upon ligand binding.

claim: HeDNA enhances histone interaction with UHRF1.
source: However, two key differences between our findings are that we show reciprocal positive allostery between the histone- and DNA-binding domains of UHRF1, and that general DNA interaction (regardless of methylation state) can displace the TTD-PHD domain and enhance histone interaction.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2A and comparison to prior work (Fang et al., 2016).

claim: General DNA interaction (regardless of methylation state) can displace the TTD-PHD domain and enhance histone interaction.
source: that general DNA interaction (regardless of methylation state) can displace the TTD-PHD domain and enhance histone interaction
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 2A and pull-down data in Figure 3B.

claim: Robust ubiquitylation of an H31-32K9me2 peptide was observed in a 20 min end-point assay in the presence of HeDNA.
source: Surprisingly, we observed robust ubiquitylation of an H31-32K9me2 peptide (Supplementary file 1) in a 20 min end-point assay in the presence of HeDNA (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4A.

claim: Neither apo-UHRF1, SyDNA, nor UnDNA could stimulate ubiquitylation activity at concentrations well above their measured Kd values.
source: Neither apo-UHRF1, SyDNA, nor UnDNA could stimulate this activity at concentrations well above their measured Kd values (Figure 4A)
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4A showing lack of activity without HeDNA.

claim: Reduced ubiquitylation activity was observed as HeDNA concentration fell below 300 nM.
source: Consistent with our measured Kd for HeDNA (Figure 1B), we observed reduced ubiquitylation activity as HeDNA concentration fell below 300 nM (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4A showing dose-dependent activity.

claim: This is the first demonstration that a DNA-protein interaction, and in particular an epigenetic modification, directly regulates enzymatic activity of an E3 ubiquitin ligase.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that a DNA-protein interaction, and in particular an epigenetic modification, directly regulates enzymatic activity of an E3 ubiquitin ligase.
evidence: This claim is based on the novelty of the finding and comparison to existing literature on E3 ligase regulation.

claim: HeDNA stimulated a 2.5-fold rate enhancement of UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation compared to UnDNA.
source: We measured a 2.5-fold rate enhancement of UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA vs. UnDNA, both in the presence or absence of H31-32K9me2 peptide (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by rate measurement data in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The rate of HeDNA-stimulated H31-32K9me2 mono-ubiquitylation was stimulated by more than 100-fold over the rate obtained with UnDNA.
source: In sharp contrast, the rate of HeDNA-stimulated H31-32K9me2 mono-ubiquitylation was stimulated by more than 100-fold over the rate obtained with UnDNA (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by rate measurement data in Figure 4B.

claim: The rate of auto-ubiquitylation was 20-fold faster than the rate of peptide ubiquitylation in the presence of UnDNA.
source: Comparing the rate of activity on UHRF1 substrates (peptide vs. self), the rate of auto-ubiquitylation was 20-fold faster than the rate of peptide ubiquitylation in the presence of UnDNA.
evidence: This claim is supported by rate measurement data in Figure 4B.

claim: The rate of peptide ubiquitylation was seven-fold faster than the rate of auto-ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA.
source: Conversely, the rate of peptide ubiquitylation was seven-fold faster than the rate of auto-ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by rate measurement data in Figure 4B.

claim: HeDNA-binding acts as an allosteric switch to enhance ubiquitylation of histone substrates.
source: Based on these observations, we propose that HeDNA-binding acts as an allosteric switch to enhance ubiquitylation of histone substrates.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the rate data in Figure 4B showing differential substrate preference with HeDNA.

claim: UHRF1 mono-, di-, and tri-ubiquitylation of purified HeLa mononucleosomes was stimulated by HeDNA.
source: Similar to peptide substrates, UHRF1 mono-, di-, and tri-ubiquitylation of purified HeLa mononucleosomes was stimulated by HeDNA (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The enhanced ubiquitylation activity of UHRF1 is relevant in the context of chromatin.
source: confirming that the enhanced ubiquitylation activity of UHRF1 is relevant in the context of chromatin
evidence: This claim is supported by mononucleosome ubiquitylation data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Excess H31-15K9me2 peptide effectively inhibited UHRF1 enzymatic activity towards mononucleosome substrates.
source: In addition, when excess H31-15K9me2 peptide (Supplementary file 1) (which harbors the TTD-PHD binding site but not the published ubiquitin target lysines) was added to UHRF1 mononucleosome ubiquitylation assays, H31-15K9me2 effectively inhibited enzymatic activity towards mononucleosome substrates (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4C showing inhibition by competing peptide.

claim: HeDNA concentrations as high as 40 μM did not block mononucleosome ubiquitylation.
source: In contrast, HeDNA concentrations as high as 40 μM did not block mononucleosome ubiquitylation, consistent with its role as an activator of UHRF1 E3 ligase activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4C showing no inhibition by HeDNA.

claim: The N-terminus of H3 is the primary binding site for substrate recognition through the TTD-PHD.
source: These results suggest that the N-terminus of H3 is the primary binding site for substrate recognition through the TTD-PHD
evidence: This claim is inferred from the peptide competition data in Figure 4C.

claim: DNA interaction can occur in trans to the nucleosome being targeted for ubiquitylation.
source: that DNA interaction can occur in trans to the nucleosome being targeted for ubiquitylation
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that excess HeDNA does not inhibit nucleosome ubiquitylation in Figure 4C.

claim: H3mut, Linkermut, DNAmut, and HeDNAmut UHRF1 exhibited defects in HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation.
source: Characterizing DNA-, HeDNA-, and histone-binding loss-of-function UHRF1 mutants in ubiquitylation assays revealed defects in HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation, with the exception of the previously reported SRA loss-of-function mutant (D469G) (Avvakumov et al., 2008)
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: D469G UHRF1 exhibited wild-type binding to HeDNA.
source: that exhibited wild-type binding to HeDNA in our assays (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization binding data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The TTD-PHD is the substrate-binding domain for HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation.
source: Ubiquitylation defects observed for H3mut and Linkermut confirmed a critical role for the TTD-PHD as the substrate-binding domain for HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4D showing loss of activity for TTD-PHD mutants.

claim: Multivalent cis engagement of H3K9me3 by the UHRF1 TTD-PHD is required for proper ubiquitylation.
source: demonstrated that multivalent cis engagement of H3K9me3 by the UHRF1 TTD-PHD is required for proper ubiquitylation (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4D showing defects for Linkermut.

claim: DNAmut UHRF1 showed complete loss of HeDNA-dependent ubiquitylation.
source: In addition, complete loss of HeDNA-dependent ubiquitylation for DNAmut UHRF1
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4D.

claim: HeDNAmut UHRF1 showed absence of multi-ubiquitylated H3.
source: the absence of multi-ubiquitylated H3 for HeDNAmut UHRF1 further support the role of DNA binding and HeDNA recognition to fully activate UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase activity
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4D.

claim: Neither ITC nor NMR spectrum intensity loss measurements indicated a change in UHRF1 affinity for E2 conjugates in the absence or presence of HeDNA.
source: Surprisingly, neither ITC nor NMR spectrum intensity loss measurements indicated a change in affinity for the E2 conjugates in the absence or presence of HeDNA (Figure 5A–B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by ITC data in Figure 5A and NMR data in Figure 5B.

claim: UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation was readily observed in the presence of HeDNA and UnDNA.
source: In addition, we readily observed UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA and UnDNA (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), indicating the RING domain of UHRF1 could productively interact with E2-ub regardless of the methylation status of the bound DNA.
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Upon UHRF1 binding to the conjugated E2, NMR resonances belonging to the conjugated ubiquitin did not suffer as great a loss in intensity.
source: Notably, upon E3 binding to the conjugated E2, NMR resonances belonging to the conjugated ubiquitin did not suffer as great a loss in intensity (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–C), indicating that ubiquitin retained its dynamics when bound to the E3.
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR data in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B-C.

claim: UHRF1 binding does not promote closed E2-ub states as strongly as other canonical RING domain E3's.
source: This observation suggests that UHRF1 binding does not promote closed E2-ub states as strongly as other canonical RING domain E3's (Christensen et al., 2007; Pruneda et al., 2011a, 2012).
evidence: This claim is inferred from NMR data in Figure 5B and comparison to prior studies on other E3 ligases.

claim: The rate of ubiquitin discharge from E2 showed only a modest increase in the reactivity of the conjugate in the presence of HeDNA.
source: The rate of ubiquitin discharge from E2 in these assays (monitored by the loss of the E2-ub and the appearance of free E2) showed only a modest increase in the reactivity of the conjugate in the presence of HeDNA (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5C.

claim: HeDNA-dependent activation of UHRF1 RING activity does not occur through enhancement of the intrinsic rate of ubiquitin discharge from the E2 to non-specific lysine sidechains.
source: These results suggest that HeDNA-dependent activation of UHRF1 RING activity does not occur through enhancement of the intrinsic rate of ubiquitin discharge from the E2 to non-specific lysine sidechains.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the modest rate increase in ubiquitin discharge assays in Figure 5C.

claim: When an H31-20 peptide was added to ubiquitin discharge reactions, rapid conversion of E2-ub to E2 was observed.
source: Remarkably, when an H31-20 peptide (Supplementary file 1) was added to ubiquitin discharge reactions, we observed rapid conversion of E2-ub to E2 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5C.

claim: The appearance of a band corresponding to ubiquitylated H31-20 was observed in ubiquitin discharge reactions with H3 peptide.
source: Additionally, we observed the appearance of a band corresponding to ubiquitylated H31-20 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5C.

claim: A decrease in the amount of free ubiquitin and UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation was observed when H3 peptide was present in ubiquitin discharge reactions.
source: Notably, we also observed a decrease in the amount of free ubiquitin and UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation formed when peptide was present, presumably because more ubiquitin was being transferred to H3 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5C.

claim: Even under conditions where free lysine was in great excess, ubiquitin was transferred rapidly and preferentially to H3 substrate in the presence of HeDNA.
source: Thus, even under conditions where free lysine was in great excess, ubiquitin was transferred rapidly and preferentially to H3 substrate in the presence of HeDNA.
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5C showing preferential H3 ubiquitylation.

claim: Neither H31-20K14acK18ac nor H31-20K9acK14acK18ac were capable of being modified with ubiquitin.
source: Neither the H31-20K14acK18ac nor H31-20K9acK14acK18ac were capable of being modified with ubiquitin (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5D showing no ubiquitylation of acetylated peptides.

claim: Rapid E2-ub depletion was only observed in the sample containing H31-20 with unblocked lysines.
source: Additionally, rapid E2-ub depletion was only observed in the sample containing H31-20 (Figure 5D), indicating that substrate binding alone does not enhance the E3 ligase activity of UHRF1 in the presence of HeDNA.
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5D.

claim: Substrate binding alone does not enhance the E3 ligase activity of UHRF1 in the presence of HeDNA.
source: indicating that substrate binding alone does not enhance the E3 ligase activity of UHRF1 in the presence of HeDNA
evidence: This claim is inferred from the ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5D showing no enhancement with acetylated peptides.

claim: Reactions that contained unblocked lysines on H31-20 accumulated less auto-ubiquitylated UHRF1 and free ubiquitin compared to assays with no peptide or with acetylated H3 peptides.
source: Consistent with our previous single turnover results (Figure 5C), reactions that contained unblocked lysines on H31-20 accumulated less auto-ubiquitylated UHRF1 and free ubiquitin compared to assays with no peptide or with the acetylated H3 peptides (Figure 5D)
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5D.

claim: HeDNA alters the substrate specificity of UHRF1 ubiquitylation.
source: supporting a model where HeDNA alters the substrate specificity of UHRF1 ubiquitylation
evidence: This claim is inferred from the ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5C-D showing preferential H3 ubiquitylation with HeDNA.

claim: Virtually no ubiquitylated species of H3 were observed in assays that lacked HeDNA.
source: It is worth noting that in all single and multiple turnover assays performed, virtually no ubiquitylated species of H3 were observed in assays that lacked HeDNA.
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitin discharge assay data in Figure 5C-D.

claim: HeDNA stimulates UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase activity through a novel regulatory mechanism.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that HeDNA stimulates UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase activity through a novel regulatory mechanism
evidence: This claim is supported by the combined data from Figures 4-5 showing HeDNA-dependent activation distinct from known E3 ligase regulatory mechanisms.

claim: HeDNA binding serves as an allosteric switch that directs the TTD-PHD bound H3 substrate to the E2-ub active site for transfer.
source: suggest that HeDNA binding serves as an allosteric switch that directs the TTD-PHD bound H3 substrate to the E2-ub active site for transfer
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined ubiquitylation and discharge assay data showing HeDNA-dependent substrate preference.

claim: The only histone peptides enriched greater than ten-fold in HeDNA samples relative to UnDNA samples were derived from H3.
source: We first identified peptides that were enriched in the HeDNA sample relative to the UnDNA sample, and the only histone peptides that were enriched greater than ten-fold were derived from H3 (Supplementary file 2)
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Supplementary file 2.

claim: Ubiquitin remnants on H3 peptides were heavily enriched in samples reacted in the presence of HeDNA relative to UnDNA.
source: Consistent with our findings that HeDNA stimulates UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase activity, ubiquitin remnants on H3 peptides were heavily enriched in samples reacted in the presence of HeDNA relative to UnDNA (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1,2).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1,2.

claim: In addition to H3K18 and H3K23, H3K14ub, H3K27ub, and H3K36ub were heavily enriched in the presence of HeDNA.
source: In addition to the previously identified sites H3K18 and H3K23, we also found H3K14ub, H3K27ub, and H3K36ub heavily enriched in the presence of HeDNA (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1,2).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1,2.

claim: Abundant H3K18ub and H3K23ub (multi-ubiquitylation) on the same peptide were identified.
source: We further identified abundant H3K18ub and H3K23ub (multi-ubiquitylation) on the same peptide.
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: H3K18ub was the most abundant ubiquitylated peptide based upon spectral counts (greater than 15-fold more than any other site).
source: H3K18ub was the most abundant ubiquitylated peptide based upon spectral counts (greater than 15-fold more than any other site)
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B.

claim: H3K23ub was only observed in the context of H3K18ub.
source: H3K23ub was only observed in the context of H3K18ub (Figure 6B)
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B.

claim: H3K18 is the preferred ubiquitylation site for UHRF1.
source: Collectively these results suggest that H3K18 is the preferred ubiquitylation site for UHRF1
evidence: This claim is inferred from mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B showing H3K18ub as the most abundant site.

claim: UHRF1 can target a number of lysines on the H3 tail for ubiquitylation.
source: but that UHRF1 can target a number of lysines on the H3 tail
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B identifying multiple ubiquitylation sites.

claim: Changes to the sites of UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation were observed in the presence of HeDNA.
source: Consistent with our model of HeDNA altering UHRF1 substrate preferences, we also observed changes to the sites of UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C-E.

claim: A nine-fold enrichment of UHRF1 K303ub was identified in the presence of HeDNA.
source: In particular, we identified a nine-fold enrichment of UHRF1 K303ub, a solvent exposed lysine in the PHD near the C-terminus of a bound H3 peptide (Figure 6—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C-D.

claim: An additional auto-ubiquitylated UHRF1 band was observed in the presence of HeDNA compared to that observed with UnDNA.
source: Accordingly, we observed an additional auto-ubiquitylated UHRF1 band in the presence of HeDNA compared to that observed with UnDNA (Figure 6—figure supplement 2E), corroborating our mass spectrometry results.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblot data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Several histone PTMs co-occurred with ubiquitylated H3 peptides, including all three states of H3K9 methylation.
source: We also identified several histone PTMs that co-occurred with ubiquitylated H3 peptides, including all three states of H3K9 methylation (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B identifying co-occurring modifications.

claim: Several of the most enriched H3 peptides not containing ubiquitin remnants also contained H3K9me2.
source: Additionally, several of the most enriched H3 peptides not containing ubiquitin remnants also contained H3K9me2 (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Supplementary file 2.

claim: Ubiquitylated H3 was detected in the presence of HeDNA (but not UnDNA) on nucleosomes marked with H3K9me3.
source: We confirmed this epigenetic link by immunoblotting HeLa mononucleosomes ubiquitylated by UHRF1. Ubiquitylated H3 was detected in the presence of HeDNA (but not UnDNA) on nucleosomes marked with H3K9me3
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblot data in Figure 6C.

claim: Ubiquitylated H3 was not detected on nucleosomes marked with H3K9acK14ac.
source: but not on nucleosomes marked with H3K9acK14ac (Figure 6C)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblot data in Figure 6C.

claim: UHRF1 could modify H2A and H2B at concentrations above 5 μM.
source: In addition, titrating recombinant human histones H3, H2A, and H2B into ubiquitylation assays revealed that while UHRF1 could modify H2A and H2B at concentrations above 5 μM
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: H3 could be modified by UHRF1 at sub-micromolar concentrations.
source: H3 could be modified at sub-micromolar concentrations
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: H3K9me2 protein could be modified by UHRF1 at even lower concentrations than unmodified H3.
source: H3K9me2 protein (synthesized by native chemical ligation) could be modified at even lower concentrations (Figure 6—figure supplement 3)
evidence: This claim is supported by ubiquitylation assay data in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: H3K9 methylation directs UHRF1 ubiquitylation to adjacent lysine residues in the presence of HeDNA.
source: Taken together, these findings strongly support the role of H3K9 methylation in directing UHRF1 ubiquitylation to adjacent lysine residues in the presence of HeDNA.
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry and immunoblot data in Figure 6B-C and Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Other histone PTMs co-occurring on ubiquitylated peptides were H3K23ac, H3K27me2, H3K36ac, and H3K37me3.
source: Other histone PTMs co-occurring on ubiquitylated peptides were: H3K23ac, also identified in another study (Qin et al., 2015); H3K27me2, which often co-occurs with H3K9me2/me3 and is considered a hallmark of facultative heterochromatin (Boros et al., 2014); H3K36ac, and H3K37me3 (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1,2).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1,2, and citations to prior studies.

claim: UHRF1 is targeted to chromatin through its coordinated histone and DNA reading activities.
source: we propose a model where UHRF1 is targeted to chromatin through its coordinated histone and DNA reading activities (Figure 7A)
evidence: This is a model claim synthesizing the binding and chromatin association data from Figures 1-3.

claim: When UHRF1 encounters HeDNA, H3 ubiquitylation serves as a mechanism to facilitate the recruitment of DNMT1 to replicating regions of the genome to copy parental DNA methylation patterns.
source: When UHRF1 encounters HeDNA, H3 ubiquitylation serves as a mechanism to facilitate the recruitment of DNMT1 to replicating regions of the genome to copy parental DNA methylation patterns (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a model claim synthesizing the ubiquitylation data from Figures 4-6 with prior knowledge of DNMT1 recruitment.

claim: HeDNA sensing is not required to target UHRF1 to bulk chromatin.
source: While it remains to be seen whether uncoupling UHRF1 from HeDNA recognition changes its residence genome-wide, our studies show HeDNA sensing is not required to target UHRF1 to bulk chromatin.
evidence: This claim is supported by chromatin association data in Figure 1D showing HeDNAmut binds chromatin.

claim: Coordinated recognition of H3 and DNA, independent of HeDNA discrimination, drives chromatin interaction.
source: Rather, coordinated recognition of H3 and DNA, independent of HeDNA discrimination, drives chromatin interaction.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the binding and chromatin association data in Figures 1-2.

claim: The avidity resulting from sub-μM affinities of UHRF1 for both DNA and H3 peptides through reciprocal positive allostery provides a biochemical basis by which UHRF1 is exclusively localized on chromatin.
source: We propose that the avidity resulting from sub-μM affinities of UHRF1 for both DNA and H3 peptides through reciprocal positive allostery provides a biochemical basis by which UHRF1 is exclusively localized on chromatin.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the binding data in Figures 1-2 showing enhanced affinities with both ligands.

claim: Small perturbations to histone binding affinity through the TTD-PHD dramatically affect chromatin targeting of UHRF1.
source: This may also explain why small perturbations to histone binding affinity through the TTD-PHD (e.g., Linkermut and TTD aromatic cage mutation [Rothbart et al., 2013, 2012]) so dramatically affect chromatin targeting of this protein.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the chromatin association data in Figure 1D and citations to prior studies.

claim: UHRF1 appears to be versatile in targeting lysines for ubiquitylation on the H3 tail.
source: UHRF1 appears to be versatile in targeting lysines for ubiquitylation on the H3 tail (Figure 6B)
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 6B identifying multiple ubiquitylation sites.

claim: UHRF1's ability to target multiple lysines may be related to the complexities of PTM patterning found on the H3 tail and the necessity to promote efficient recruitment of DNMT1 to differentially modified chromatin environments.
source: this ability may be related to the complexities of PTM patterning found on this region of the H3 tail (Young et al., 2009) and the necessity to promote efficient recruitment of DNMT1 to differentially modified chromatin environments
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the mass spectrometry data and citation to prior work on PTM complexity.

claim: UHRF1 histone ubiquitylation may serve other roles in DNA related processes (i.e., DNA repair).
source: In addition, UHRF1 histone ubiquitylation may serve other roles in DNA related processes (i.e., DNA repair) (Liang et al., 2015; Tian et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on citations to prior studies linking UHRF1 to DNA repair.

claim: DNMT1 has an intrinsic preference for HeDNA substrates.
source: Important to note are studies on the enzymology of DNMT1 activity that show the enzyme has an intrinsic preference for HeDNA substrates (Goyal et al., 2006)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior enzymatic studies of DNMT1.

claim: DNMT1 methylates in a processive manner.
source: methylates in a processive manner (Bestor and Ingram, 1983; Hermann et al., 2004)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior enzymatic studies of DNMT1.

claim: UHRF1 functions to provide a nucleation event for DNMT1 recruitment to chromatin.
source: Considering DNMT1 behavior on oligonucleotide substrates, it is intriguing to speculate that UHRF1 functions to provide a nucleation event for DNMT1 recruitment to chromatin.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the combined data and knowledge of DNMT1 processivity.

claim: HeDNA is bound by the UHRF1 SRA in a manner that positions the RING in proximity to the H3 binding region of UHRF1.
source: We speculate that HeDNA is bound by the UHRF1 SRA in a manner that positions the RING in proximity to the H3 binding region of UHRF1.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the ubiquitylation data and structural considerations.

claim: RING activity towards H3 may be conformationally restricted when UHRF1 binds SyDNA or UnDNA.
source: RING activity towards H3 may be conformationally restricted when UHRF1 binds SyDNA or UnDNA (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the differential ubiquitylation activity with different DNA substrates.

claim: Structures of the SRA domain from mouse UHRF1 (Np95) show this domain can adopt different conformations bound to UnDNA and HeDNA.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, structures of the SRA domain from mouse UHRF1 (Np95) show this domain can adopt different conformations bound to UnDNA and HeDNA (Figure 7—figure supplement 1) (Hashimoto et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior structural studies and reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The NKR finger of the UHRF1 SRA adopts a highly ordered conformation upon HeDNA binding.
source: Also the NKR finger of the UHRF1 SRA, which harbors the HeDNAmut, adopts a highly ordered conformation upon HeDNA binding (Avvakumov et al., 2008; Hashimoto et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior structural studies.

claim: The stable finger conformation upon HeDNA binding is critical for HeDNA-stimulated H3 ubiquitylation.
source: This allows for pseudo-base pairing to the exposed guanosine nucleotide (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), and we hypothesize this stable finger conformation is critical for HeDNA-stimulated H3 ubiquitylation.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on structural information and ubiquitylation data.

claim: The half-life of H2BK123ub in budding yeast is approximately one minute.
source: In fact, recent analysis of ubiquitin turnover kinetics showed that the half-life of H2BK123ub in budding yeast is approximately one minute (Yumerefendi et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a prior study on ubiquitin turnover.

claim: USP7 may be responsible for removing H3 ubiquitylation through interaction with DNMT1.
source: The initial study implicating H3 ubiquitylation in the inheritance of DNA methylation indirectly suggested that USP7 may be responsible for this function through interaction with DNMT1 (Nishiyama et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on citation to a prior study.

claim: USP7 has been shown to interact with UHRF1.
source: This is notable, as USP7 has also been shown to interact with UHRF1 (Zhang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a prior study.

claim: Recent studies have tied USP7 to DNA replication and the maintenance of heterochromatin.
source: Additionally, recent studies have tied USP7 to DNA replication (Lecona et al., 2016) and the maintenance of heterochromatin (Mungamuri et al., 2016), providing a biological link to replication-coupled inheritance of DNA methylation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Direct evidence of USP7 catalyzed deubiquitylation of H3 is lacking.
source: However direct evidence of USP7 catalyzed deubiquitylation of H3 is lacking.
evidence: This claim is based on assessment of the existing literature.
